text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenneth Matiba, chairman of opposition FORD-Asili party says he does not recognise an opposition-backed alliance lobbying for constitutional reforms.
- Some members of parliament from the ruling party are meet on Wednesday to discuss the agenda for political reforms, a move that may indicate differences within the party.
- Attorney-General Amos Wako discloses he is drafting a bill to establish an anti-corruption authority to investigate high-level corruption by politically-connected individuals.
- Official opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa receives a rousing welcome in Garissa town in northeastern Kenya.
- Emmanuel Maitha, a ruling party activist, says he will disrupt all pro-reform rallies held in the coast province.
- Two brothers are sentenced to a total of three years in prison for escaping from police custody.
- Thousands of lives could be in danger following an influx of counterfeit and adulterated drugs into the country.
- Kenyan police authorities say the ongoing swoop on illegal aliens in Nairobi is not aimed at Rwandan nationals. ($1=59 Kenyan Shillings)
